parsing_rationale: The document was analyzed by separating the actual project content (Football Match Manager) from the template placeholders (e.g., [PRINCIPLE_1_NAME]). I extracted the core principles as requirements and the development workflow as rules and testing gates. The mapping follows the strict template fields provided, and structural gaps were identified for missing coding standards and open questions.

project_info.brief_explanation: Technical constitution defining core principles and development workflow for a football match management application.

sections.title: I. User-Centric Design
sections.raw_content: Every feature must prioritize the user's experience and needs, ensuring that the app is intuitive and valuable for football fans.

sections.title: II. Data Reliability
sections.raw_content: Match data must be accurate and up-to-date, sourced from reliable providers.

sections.title: III. Simplicity and Performance
sections.raw_content: The application should be fast and lightweight, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

sections.title: IV. Extensibility
sections.raw_content: The system should be designed to allow for easy addition of new features and leagues.

sections.title: V. Open Standards
sections.raw_content: Use open standards and technologies where possible to ensure longevity and flexibility.

sections.title: VI. Test-First Development
sections.raw_content: TDD mandatory: Tests written → User approved → Tests fail → Then implement; Red-Green-Refactor cycle strictly enforced.

sections.title: VII. Code Review
sections.raw_content: All code changes must be reviewed by at least one other team member before merging.

sections.title: Governance
sections.raw_content:
This constitution supersedes all other practices. Amendments require documentation, approval, and a migration plan if affecting existing data.

**Version**: 0.1.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-07-30 | **Last Amended**: 2026-07-30
